changeSet.author: claude (P4-13)
changeSet.comment: Publisher display names (decided 2026-10-03): listings show them, browse can search them, and listings whose publisher has no name are hidden. A copy of ms_user's display_name kept current by user.profile.updated (rule 5 - no call to ms_user at request time). keycloak_id is the JWT subject, the same value dictionary_stats.fk_user_id holds; no FK either way, because a listing can arrive before its publisher's name. display_name is nullable: null = the user has no name now, and the row stays so its source_updated_at rejects older events (rule 4). VARCHAR(255) matches ms_user's column. The name filter is a case-insensitive substring match (lower(display_name) LIKE '%...%'), which only a trigram index can serve, so pg_trgm is installed and the GIN index is on lower(display_name), the exact expression the query uses. pg_trgm is a trusted extension on Postgres 13+, so a database owner can create it without superuser. The rollback leaves the extension installed: dropping it could break anything else that started using it.

sql.sql: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;
CREATE INDEX idx_publishers_display_name_trgm ON publishers USING GIN (lower(display_name) gin_trgm_ops);
